chains.title: The Common Passage
chains.summary: A merchant fails to arrive. Tobin asks you to investigate the Kelp Reach shipping routes. The rescue guarantee brings Della Venn into the dispute.

stages.title: Overdue Merchant
stages.body:
Tobin Hale: ‘A merchant out of Kelp Reach missed its berth. The departure report is dated; I cannot tell you where it is now. Find a loaded independent convoy and bring its passage safely into harbor. Take a paid escort only after its captain shows you the actual terms.’

You can keep your Tinwake and your other work. The client pays from its own operating purse after delivery. Your wages, fuel and repairs remain your costs.
stages.nextAction: Review the Kelp Reach route and return allowance. Approach a peaceful loaded merchant, accept its escort and remain within 600 units.

stages.title: Escort a loaded merchant
stages.body: Keep the original loaded boats together until they sell their cargo at the named harbor. Any interception requires their physical escape. Losing a carrier, leaving the protection radius or withdrawing ends the contract under its normal refund rules. You can seek another actual client after closing a failed passage.
stages.nextAction: Collect the bound client's escort fee at the delivery harbor, then return to Tobin at Brass Haven.

choices.text: Report the completed passage to Tobin

stages.title: The rescue guarantee
stages.body:
Tobin Hale: ‘The cargo arrived. The merchant's fee is yours. This claim is separate.’

Tobin opens a notice from Della Venn, the Compact's charter administrator. ‘My wardens keep these routes open. A captain who asks for rescue accepts our service terms. Your escort does not cancel the earlier debt.’

Tobin recognizes the countersignature. He financed the guarantee when the harbors needed protection; he did not tell you how a missed payment could transfer control of a boat.
stages.nextAction: Ask Tobin why his signature appears on Venn’s guarantee.

choices.text: Ask who authorized the seizure terms

consequences.reason: Returned with a paid escort's actual delivery and questioned the rescue guarantee

stages.title: Second Signature
stages.body:
Tobin lays Venn's notice beside a harbor bounty. ‘The raiders named in these claims collected under my guarantee. I financed it. I thought I was paying for protection. Find their original boats, then keep what you can recover or secure. A bounty paid for someone else's victory will not tell us what happened aboard them.’

Take only the harbor's existing funded contract. After a physical encounter, paid fitting recovery or an intact captured hull can establish original property. Its identity and your current custody matter. If the source is actually lost, report that outcome plainly; the investigation creates no replacement boat or prize.
stages.nextAction: Review the actual bounty, reacquire its boats through the coastal watch, and bring original secured property to a harbor. Claim or withdraw the contract before sending Tobin the report.

choices.text: Send Tobin the report with secured original property
Explicitly report that no original property is retained
choices.tradeoff: Available only after actual loss or a paid public defeat confirmation. This awards no property and makes no claim that you witnessed someone else's battle.

stages.title: Tobin's countersignature
stages.body:
Tobin replies in writing: ‘I checked the seizure clause against my guarantee. It permits the administrator to take control of a boat after an unpaid rescue claim. My signature made that enforceable. Public money stood behind it.’

‘I kept saying we needed the next convoy protected. That did not entitle me to hide these terms from its captain. Wren is trying to get working boats out of Kelp Reach. She needs to know what I signed before she asks anyone to rely on a different promise.’
stages.nextAction: Keep the actual property or recorded loss, and read the lead concerning Wren and Kelp Reach.

consequences.reason: Required Tobin to acknowledge his funded guarantee and its seizure terms

stages.title: Exit Channel
stages.body:
Wren writes from Reedwater Floats: ‘The working boats at Kelp Reach are trying to leave. Stay with them while they are exposed. Chasing an enemy that turns away leaves their passage uncovered.’

‘Protection crews need wages too. That does not excuse impounding a boat. I must explain how the next escort will be paid for when I ask people to reject Venn’s guarantee. First, find the boats already moving out.’
stages.nextAction: Approach a loaded convoy leaving Kelp Reach and review its funded escort and your reserves.

stages.title: Cover the working boats
stages.body: Keep the original working boats covered as they leave Kelp. During an interception, boats must reach the physical exit. A quiet passage can clear at its actual harbor. The journal records each boat separately, including losses and boats whose withdrawal remains unconfirmed.
stages.nextAction: Account for the original boats, then claim or withdraw the escort contract and send Wren the report from a harbor.

stages.title: Wren’s account
stages.body:
Wren accepts your list of the original boats and the outcomes you could confirm. She records arrivals, escapes and losses separately. A sunken hull cannot appear among the boats that got clear.

‘Their owners still have crews to pay and fuel to buy. Those costs belong in the account too. Mara at Anvil Dock needs repair materials brought to Cinder Quay. Venn says her wardens keep some of those routes open. Check what they actually protect before deciding what should replace them.’
stages.nextAction: Read Mara’s repair-material lead.

stages.title: A Useful Enemy
stages.body:
A letter from Mara waits at Cinder Quay with a repair list. "Venn says her patrols keep these routes open. Bring the kits; I need to know who pays for the next sailing."

Anvil Dock can commission a public shipment of eight repair kits from its existing stores. Review the funded quantity, materials invoice and delivery fee there. Your fleet still pays its own wages, fuel and repairs.
stages.nextAction: Read the repair request, then review the order at Anvil Dock.

choices.text: I will review the order at Anvil Dock.

stages.title: Repair Materials
stages.body: Review the public order at Anvil Dock before accepting it. Bring any accepted freight to Cinder Quay and deliver it through the harbor service. If the freight is lost, you withdraw, or the request cannot be filled, tell Mara how the run ended.
stages.nextAction: Review the order, then report its outcome.

choices.text: Tell Mara what happened to the kits.

stages.title: The Materials Account
stages.body:
Your report is filed for Mara. Her instructions remain with the order: "The kits are part of it. The people fitting them need wages, and the next sailing needs fuel. I need an alternative that can pay those costs."

Her letter refers you to Cass at Rust Anchorage, who knows how the seized routes were sold.
stages.nextAction: Read Cass's Rust Anchorage lead.

stages.title: Bought Route
stages.body:
Cass meets you at Rust Anchorage. "I sold the route. I knew the buyers meant to stop a boat. I took the money anyway."

Cass names the Rust crews that used it. "What they still hold may have changed. Find the actual boats before you agree to a price or risk your crew. I cannot promise what is left."
stages.nextAction: Hear Cass, then inspect a currently observed Rust raider.

stages.title: The Held Property
stages.body:
Cass’s information points to the Rust raiders. A release buys only the actual cargo shown in its terms. It does not settle other claims against the crew.

For a raid, retain an original captured hull or recover an original fitting from its wreck, then withdraw to another lawful harbor with it. A battle result by itself brings nothing home.
stages.nextAction: Inspect a current Rust contact. Review a release or recover original property, then report from a harbor.

choices.text: Report the release or recovered property.
choices.tradeoff: Requires a completed paid release, or original raid property retained after sailing to another lawful harbor.

choices.text: Close this attempt without a recovery.
choices.tradeoff: Records no recovery or reward. Unconfirmed property remains unconfirmed; the existing crews and their property remain in the world.

stages.title: Cass’s Account
stages.body:
You send Cass the outcome. Her reply is short: "I will give the witnesses the same account. I knew what the route could be used for. What you managed afterward does not change what I sold."

Wren is gathering the people willing to speak. Their destination must be agreed before anyone boards.
stages.nextAction: Read Wren’s Reedwater Floats lead.

stages.title: Names on Paper
stages.body:
At Reedwater Floats, Wren opens a letter from Rust Anchorage. Two residents who saw the collections are willing to give an account. Cass has agreed to introduce them.

"Agree where they will be received before anyone boards," Wren says. "Here, they can testify before the public clerks. Mara can arrange protected reception at Anvil Dock instead. The harbor still needs berths, provisions and paid reception workers."
stages.nextAction: Choose the destination, then collect the two witnesses at Rust Anchorage.

choices.tradeoff: The agreed destination is Reedwater Floats. Their account enters a public hearing.
The agreed destination is Anvil Dock. Keep their identities out of the public account.

stages.title: Witness Passage
stages.body:
The two places must be on an actual boat, with food aboard and a funded reception at the agreed destination. Review the terms before boarding.

Once they embark, their existing savings and provisions travel with the cohort. If the passage cannot continue, use the normal recall and return arrangements. Reaching the destination begins reception; it does not finish the hearing.
stages.nextAction: Board at Rust Anchorage, sail to the agreed reception, and complete its two service days.

choices.tradeoff: Requires the actual cohort’s completed discharge, return or loss settlement. An unaccepted passage can be reported as unfilled; passengers aboard cannot be discarded by this report.

stages.title: The Witness Account
stages.body:
You send Wren the outcome and the paid costs. She keeps that account beside Cass’s admission. The record separates the agreed destination from what actually happened on the voyage.

Another message reaches the harbor: loaded boats on the Kelp routes have reported danger. Their owners still have to decide what they can afford to protect.
stages.nextAction: Read the Kelp distress lead.

stages.title: Two Distress Flags
stages.body:
At Kelp Reach, the signal clerk opens requests for cover from the coastal cargo boats. The reports name their owners, loads and last observed positions. Their captains are still underway.

Choose which passage to cover first. The other boats will continue under their own captain; accepting one request does not reserve the other convoy or its cargo.
stages.nextAction: Review two distinct reported passages and accept one current funded escort.

choices.tradeoff: Keep the original boats, surviving load and existing escort terms.

stages.title: Narrow Withdrawal
stages.body:
The contracted boats still have a harbor to reach. Stay alongside their withdrawal or turn toward an actual pursuer. The held fee covers the contracted delivery; your fuel, crew wages and repairs remain operating costs.

The signal clerk needs an account of the original boats. Unseen boats have an unconfirmed fate until an arrival record or an observed encounter establishes what happened.
stages.nextAction: Cover the remaining passage or interdict a pursuer; settle the native contract before reporting.

choices.tradeoff: Confirmed arrivals, physical exits, losses and unconfirmed boats remain separate from the escort fee.

stages.title: The Convoy Account
stages.body:
You send the passage account to Kelp Reach. Wren keeps the confirmed arrivals and losses beside the unresolved reports. No second payment has been promised for the same passage.

Mara asks you to meet at Anvil Dock. Tobin has proposed paid escort obligations to replace Venn’s guarantee. Before the next sailing, the harbors must decide which accounts will fund it.
stages.nextAction: Read Mara’s request about funding the next escort.

stages.title: Who Pays First
stages.body:
Mara lays Tobin’s revised terms across her workbench. He wants each boat owner to commission and bond its own escort. Wren has sent a second proposal: the departure and receiving harbors share the escort fee from their separate local budgets.

"Tobin wants each owner to post its own bond," Mara says. "Wren wants both harbors to pay. You’ll be the one meeting the captains. Choose the terms you can offer them."

Review the cost of the first passage before signing it. Your crew wages, fuel, provisions and repairs remain your responsibility.
stages.nextAction: Choose the funding terms at Anvil Dock.

choices.tradeoff: The departure and receiving harbors each contribute a disclosed share from their own budgets, subject to available coins. Unused refunded contributions remain owed to their original harbors.
Each convoy owner pays the held escort fee from its own operating purse. Harbor budgets do not contribute.

stages.title: The First Funded Escort
stages.body:
Find a loaded convoy whose captain can offer a passage under the agreed terms. Check the original boats, cargo, fee and payer before accepting.

Stay with the contracted delivery. If the passage fails, close the native escort account and review what was returned and what remains owed before reporting.
stages.nextAction: Review a current funded escort and carry out the agreed passage.

choices.tradeoff: The account must distinguish a paid delivery, an unearned refund and any unsettled harbor contribution.

stages.title: The Funding Account
stages.body:
Mara sends the account to the harbor clerks with the terms you chose. The payer, held fee and settlement are recorded against that passage.

Tobin replies with a report of selective stops around Naphtha Bay’s fuel routes. The sellers still control their own stock. He asks you to check what passage is available before he promises the next sailing.
stages.nextAction: Read Tobin’s report from Naphtha Bay.

stages.title: Fuel Has Owners
stages.body:
At Naphtha Bay, Tobin's report of selective stops lies beside the current harbor terms. A report is not a reason to pay for permission you already have. Check whether ordinary entry is lawful today before buying safe conduct.

Mara has added a note: "Getting through the entrance doesn't buy the seller's fuel. Ask what is for sale, and what it costs."

Tobin has written beneath it: "Venn kept supplies moving when we could not. Replacing her terms still means paying the people who do that work."
stages.nextAction: Review Naphtha's current entry terms, then the fuel seller's price.

choices.text: Check the entry terms and fuel offer.
choices.tradeoff: Lawful entry costs no permission fee. If paid safe conduct is needed, its disclosed charge buys three days of port-specific permission, not fuel or protection at sea.

stages.title: The Seller's Stock
stages.body:
The entry terms and the fuel invoice belong on separate lines. Review the stock offered for sale, your hold space and the price before ordering. Passing the harbor does not place fuel aboard.

You can buy a small quantity or leave the offer alone. Any passage charge, purchase and later operating costs remain expenses of this voyage.
stages.nextAction: Review the purchase record before reporting at Naphtha Bay.

choices.text: Enter the fuel purchase in the account.
choices.tradeoff: Report the dated purchase and its paid price. Permission alone, or fuel already aboard, cannot stand in for the seller's receipt.

stages.title: The Fuel Account
stages.body:
Mara copies the purchase into the voyage book and leaves the entry-permission charge on a separate line. "The fuel came from someone's stock," she says. "It has a price whether we agree with Venn or not."

Tobin asks you to return to Brass Haven. He wants a way to hear a request for protection without signing away another boat. The earlier guarantees and their disputed obligations remain on the books.
stages.nextAction: Read Tobin's request, then return to Brass Haven.

choices.text: Read the request from Brass Haven.
choices.tradeoff: A protection request does not establish a right to payment or prove what its applicant did under an earlier guarantee.

stages.title: Last Warrant
stages.body:
At Brass Haven, Tobin has ruled a place for the date and boat on a fresh application. Any applicant must be identified from the current coastal watch. A claim to protection under a guarantee will be entered as unverified.

"I won't promise an escort we cannot pay for," he says. "Some people asking may owe us answers. I still won't use an accusation as a reason to abandon a crew."

Venn's protection has carried useful cargo as well as disputed claims. A completed passage can establish what happened to one load. It cannot decide every earlier accusation.
stages.nextAction: Review the current boats and funded passages near Brass Haven.

choices.tradeoff: Only an existing loaded convoy with an affordable escort offer can be accepted. Without one, keep watching or report the request unresolved at Brass Haven.

stages.title: A Passage to Account For
stages.body:
Keep the applicant's statement beside the passage record, not in place of it. Check the owner, original loaded boats, destination, held fee and your own operating reserves.

A paid delivery establishes that contracted passage. A failed, unavailable or unseen passage remains unresolved; it proves neither rescue nor guilt. You may continue the coastal watch instead of closing the request.
stages.nextAction: Review the passage record; report a paid delivery or an unresolved request at Brass Haven.

choices.text: Report the paid passage at Brass Haven.
choices.tradeoff: Requires the original contracted delivery, sale and collected escort fee. This receipt establishes the passage, not the applicant's earlier claims.

choices.text: Report the request unresolved at Brass Haven.
choices.tradeoff: Available at Brass Haven after any carried escort is closed. Record the missing or unsuccessful passage without claiming a rescue, payment or finding of guilt.

stages.title: The Warrant Account
stages.body:
Tobin reviews your account. “I’ll enter what you can show,” he says. “A paid delivery has its receipt. An unsuccessful passage keeps its outcome. A request without a contracted boat stays unresolved.”

If an application was recorded, he keeps its unverified claims separate from the observed outcome. The costs already incurred and the obligations already recorded remain.

The next proposal concerns a common passage beyond this coast. That sailing still needs its own funding.
stages.nextAction: Keep this account and read the next passage proposal.

choices.tradeoff: This preserves the current account. It buys no boat, cargo or later passage and cancels no debt.

stages.title: Common Passage
stages.body: The next campaign operation is not available in this version. Your voyage book and outstanding obligations remain; ordinary harbor work can continue.
stages.nextAction: Continue other harbor work.

gate.message: The next campaign operation is not available in this version.

chains.title: Tobin: The guarantee
chains.summary: Ask Tobin to read the seizure clause, or explain why he signed it. This optional conversation does not gate the campaign.

stages.title: Read It Aloud
stages.body:
Tobin sets the guarantee on the desk. ‘We were keeping boats moving. I thought the limits were obvious.’

You can ask him to read the seizure authority without paraphrasing, or explain why he accepted it. Hearing him out does not commit you to his explanation.
stages.nextAction: Choose what to ask Tobin.

choices.text: Ask Tobin to read the seizure clause as written
Ask why Tobin signed the guarantee

stages.title: Tobin's answer
stages.body:
Tobin reads the authority allowing an unpaid rescue claim to become control of the boat. He stops at his own signature.

‘I was afraid no one would back the next sailing. I signed wider powers than I could justify. When people asked what the guarantee meant, I argued about the boats we had already saved.’

He leaves the paper where you can read it. You do not have to accept his explanation, forgive him or buy anything.
stages.nextAction: End this conversation whenever you are ready.

stages.title: Who Can Pay
stages.body:
Tobin turns back to the seizure clause he read to you. "I signed it. When people asked what we could take, I answered with the sailings we'd kept alive. That didn't make the powers I signed any narrower."

This time he asks who can pay before asking a captain to sail. He offers to read the funding terms already chosen for the recent escort. There is no new commission on the desk. You can leave without buying anything.
stages.nextAction: Read the existing funding account with Tobin, or leave.

choices.tradeoff: Discuss only the recorded funding terms, payments and remaining obligations. This orders no escort and transfers no coins.
No purchase, payment or new commission is required.

stages.title: Before Asking a Captain
stages.body:
Tobin reads the recorded payer and terms before saying what he wants the next captain to do. Harbor contributions belong to those harbors; an owner's bond comes from that owner's purse. Neither supplies the escort captain's wages, provisions or repairs.

"If the money isn't there, I have to say so before I ask them to go," he says. "And if something is still owed, I can't call it settled just because I've written another offer."

He makes no payment during this conversation. His earlier signature and explanation stay in the record.
stages.nextAction: Finish the conversation when ready.

choices.text: Keep the account and finish the conversation.
choices.tradeoff: The conversation adds no commission and changes no outstanding balance.

chains.title: Mara: repair work
chains.summary: Talk with Mara about repair materials and the people who fit them.

stages.title: The Repair Quote
stages.body: Mara looks toward your boats. "Which hull needs attention? The harbor can give you an estimate for the kits and the work." She waits while you consider the price.
stages.nextAction: Review the estimate or ask about the work.

choices.text: How do you price the work?

stages.title: Terms for the Work
stages.body: "Some repairs need more skilled hands than others," Mara says. "The kits come from the stores, and the people fitting them need wages. Ask what the whole job costs before you commission it."
stages.nextAction: Finish the conversation when ready.

stages.title: A Boat at the Quay
stages.body:
Mara leaves the account with her clerk and comes down to the quay. "Which boat do you want me to look at?"

Choose one of your damaged boats for a repair estimate. You can leave without ordering work.
stages.nextAction: Choose a damaged boat for an estimate, or leave.

choices.tradeoff: Requires a selected boat you own, present at Anvil Dock, with damage that the yard can quote. No repair is ordered.

choices.text: Leave the inspection for another time.

stages.title: The Repair Estimate
stages.body:
Mara marks the damage beside the boat’s name and itemizes the estimate. Materials, expert work and harbor charges remain separate costs.

"The estimate is here when you need it," she says. "The yard still needs the supplies before work can begin."
stages.nextAction: Review the estimate; repair work remains a separate order.

choices.text: Keep the estimate and finish the conversation.

chains.title: Cass: the route sale
chains.summary: Ask Cass what she knew when she sold the route.

stages.title: The Price of Directions
stages.body: Cass offers to tell you what the buyer paid. "Would the amount make a difference to you?"
stages.nextAction: Ask what Cass knew.

choices.text: What did you know the buyer intended?

stages.title: What Cass Knew
stages.body: "They meant to stop that boat. I knew it, and I sold the route anyway." Cass puts the tally away. "You can hear that without forgiving it. I will stop offering useful information as if it repays them."
stages.nextAction: Finish the conversation when ready.

choices.text: Keep Cass’s admission in the account.

chains.title: Wren: the testimony
chains.summary: Talk with Wren after the witnesses have completed their agreed reception.

stages.title: Hearing the Account
stages.body: Wren checks the reception account. "They have been received, and the work is paid for. Now the clerks can hear what they saw." She places a clean sheet beside the ledger. "We can record the costs without putting protected names into the public copy."
stages.nextAction: Finish the conversation when ready.

choices.text: Keep the cost account with the testimony.
